- [ ] With `ansible_local` provisioner configured, can you successfully apply the following steps?

```
$ vagrant up --no-provision
...
$ vagrant ssh
```

Many thanks in advance!

@vikas027 thank you for the additional details. Now things are quite clear, I think (the first log excerpts was indeed not pointing the issue).

By using Ansible 2.0+, you're affected by the ansible/ansible#12004 regression. This has been tracked by issue #6793 and fixed by #6869. Unfortunately this can only be resolved in the next Vagrant release, or in future versions of Ansible.

You have (at least) two possible workarounds:
- Adapt your Packer configuration to install an Ansible 1.9 version instead (e.g. `sudo pip install ansible==1.9.4`)
- If for some reason you really need to run Ansible 2.0+, then you can manually patch your current Vagrant 1.8.1 installation(s) (it's only one word to add, see https://github.com/mitchellh/vagrant/commit/9dbdb9397a92d4fc489e9afcb022621df7f60d11)

I hope you can find a quick fix that suits your situation, and that we can get better integration between Ansible 2.0 and Vagrant "very soon" :-)

@gildegoma Thank you for the super quick response. 

I am forced to use Ansible 2.0+ since my playbooks are dependent on it. It would be quite a pain to make it backwards compatible.

My Virtualbox issue has been fixed via [9dbdb93](https://github.com/mitchellh/vagrant/commit/9dbdb9397a92d4fc489e9afcb022621df7f60d11). I've modified file `/opt/vagrant/embedded/gems/gems/vagrant-1.8.1/plugins/provisioners/ansible/provisioner/guest.rb` on OSX
and `/usr/lib/python2.6/site-packages/ansible/cli/galaxy.py` on the guest OS as suggested in [11b55be](https://github.com/ansible/ansible/commit/11b55be5bbb90b2bc917b2637d6fcdbe1a15092d).

But my AWS issue still persists. I cannot run any vagrant command if I have `ansible_local` in Vagranfile, even before running `vagrant up`; error is same as above.
@vikas027 thanks for the additional details. Then I'll try with AWS next week and give you some feedbacks.

So far, I haven't investigated to figure out how the `vagrant-aws` provider does behave to generate this situation. For instance, the `vagrant-digitalocean` provider doesn't enter in a such dead loop and works fine for me (with the 4e451c6e991e96fc0f1968004581c3861725b053 fix).

Anyway, #6763 already showed that it was probably a bad idea of mine to assume that SSH communication is possible during the `config` stage of a provisioner plugin. As this configuration check step occurs before the execution of each vagrant command, it will more robust (and faster) to never try to perform any SSH communication during this stage (missing file errors will be finally raised by Ansible during the `provision` stage).

@vikas027 for now, you can easily patch your Vagrant 1.8.1 installation with the following workaround:

Replace the [original Config::Guest::check_path()](https://github.com/mitchellh/vagrant/blob/v1.8.1/plugins/provisioners/ansible/config/guest.rb#L39-L50) by this dummy implementation:

``` ruby
  def check_path(machine, path, test_args, error_message_key = nil)
    true
  end
```
I renamed the issue to focus on the AWS bug, as the "Virtualbox" use case above is actually tracked by #6793.

body:
@sethvargo can you please confirm (or infirm) the following statements:

The _Config_ module of a Vagrant plugin shouldn't generate remote interactions with the guest system.

**Main Reason:**

The "Configuration Check" stage is thought to validate "things" that are available on the Vagrant Host, not on the guests.

---

I know that `plugins/provisioners/ansible/config/guest.rb` is currently the only `config` place where `machine.communicate` operations occur (compared to other core provisioners), which already answers quite well the above question. But I'd prefer to get an expert blame :smiley:
